items.title: Iran Issues List of Demands, Dampening Hopes of Reopening Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: The head of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council said that the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed until the United States met certain conditions.

items.title: Yemen Teeters on Civil War as Regional Stability Hangs in the Balance
items.summary: While the Middle East waits to hear whether a deal can be reached to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the Yemeni government’s conflict with Iran-backed Houthi rebels escalated overnight.

items.title: Whirling Like Dervishes in Turkey, but Open to Everyone
items.summary: Hundreds of people attended a seven-day retreat in the Turkish countryside seeking transcendence through sema, the spiritual practice of whirling.

items.title: As Thailand Gets Known for Mass Shootings, Fresh Pledges to Fix Gun Laws
items.summary: A rampage at a high school in Thailand on Friday was the latest episode of gun violence in a country that has grappled in recent years with several attacks.

items.title: Bald Range Wildfire Forces Evacuation of 18,000 in British Columbia
items.summary: The Bald Range fire has burned more than 25,000 acres in British Columbia. At one point, the fire spread more than 2,000 acres in about an hour, officials said.

items.title: Canada Wildfires: What to Know About Fires in British Columbia and Ontario
items.summary: Wildfire activity has increased in British Columbia, with thousands evacuated from the Okanagan Valley, weeks after smoke from blazes in Ontario choked the East Coast.

items.title: Pellet Guns, Sticks and Tear Gas: How India’s Police Halted a Youth March
items.summary: A New York Times analysis details the July 20 crackdown on unarmed protesters in New Delhi that has provoked public outrage and accusations of excessive force.

items.title: Their African Islands Were Set to Be Decolonized. Then the U.S. Bombed Iran.
items.summary: The inhabitants of the Chagos Islands were expelled by the British 60 years ago. Refugees were anxious to return this year, but their hopes have been caught in a morass of geopolitics.

items.title: As Ukraine Strikes Wildberries, Russia’s Richest Businesswoman Faces Her Biggest Test Yet
items.summary: As Ukraine repeatedly strikes warehouses of the e-commerce site Wildberries, Tatyana Kim, its billionaire co-founder, faces her biggest test yet.

items.title: Italy’s Heat Will Spread to Western Europe Ahead of Solar Eclipse
items.summary: Red high-temperature warnings remained in effect for much of southern and western Italy through Saturday.

items.title: MacKenzie Scott Steps Back Into Spotlight With New Book
items.summary: She posted four pages of a manuscript on a newly started Substack newsletter on Saturday and said that the novel would be released serially throughout August.

items.title: Think It’s Cool to Wear Fancy Sneakers to Work? You Might Be Old.
items.summary: After years of office casual, young people are embracing loafers, derbies and oxfords.

items.title: Medicare Advantage’s Perks Are Getting Scrutiny
items.summary: Officials said no to health plans that wanted to expand extra benefits to cover medical marijuana, streaming services and shopping clubs. More changes are coming in 2027.

items.title: How an N.F.L.-Backed Plan to Revitalize Canton, Ohio, Faltered
items.summary: The “Hall of Fame Village” was pitched in 2014 as a boon to the city. But hundreds of millions were spent, the N.F.L. backed out, and the project is unfinished.

items.title: Can Netflix Save a Summer Slump With a Stunt on Sunset Boulevard?
items.summary: The streaming giant, still looking for this year’s blockbuster, paid an actor to spend three days inside a billboard in Los Angeles to promote an upcoming film.

items.title: Canada Offers U.S. Concessions in Trade Talks but Demands a Comprehensive Deal
items.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney is attempting to prevent 50 percent tariffs against many Canadian goods scheduled for this month.

items.title: Trump Restarts Battle to Fire Sitting Fed Governor Lisa Cook
items.summary: The Trump administration, rebuffed by the Supreme Court in its first attempt to fire Lisa D. Cook, sent the Federal Reserve governor a letter saying it was “considering” removing her from the job.

items.title: Weak Jobs Report Does Not Eliminate Prospects of Interest Rate Rise
items.summary: Officials at the Federal Reserve are chiefly focused on the trajectory of inflation after five years of overshooting the central bank’s 2 percent target.

items.title: If You’re Struggling to Pay Day-to-Day Bills, There’s Help
items.summary: Nonprofit financial counselors say there has been a significant increase this year in the number of borrowers seeking their advice.

items.title: The Bond Market Is Signaling Rising Risks. Investors Should Listen.
items.summary: While the Fed didn’t raise rates, the bond market did. That means hardship for home buyers and higher hurdles for A.I. data centers and the stock market. But it’s also a boon for retirees.

items.title: Meta Ordered to Pay $567 Million Fine by New Mexico Judge
items.summary: The penalty, imposed by a state judge, is on top of a $375 million fine ordered by a jury that found Meta misled users about the safety of its platforms.

items.title: China’s Unitree Prices IPO in Bet Investors Are Ready for Humanoid Robots
items.summary: Unitree Robotics wants to raise about $900 million in an I.P.O. that tests market interest in humanoid robots, a technology that wows but has yet to prove its viability.

items.title: Google Names Demis Hassabis to New AI Role in a Leadership Shake-up
items.summary: Minutes after four top researchers said they were leaving, Google said that Demis Hassabis, the Nobel-winning scientist who led the company’s A.I. lab, was stepping into a new job.

items.title: The White House’s Secret A.I. Rules + The State of Model Alignment With METR’s Chris Painter + The Final Hot Mess Express
items.summary: A few details from the White House’s A.I. plan have leaked to the news media, but the administration has officially communicated almost nothing.

items.title: New Amazon Data Center Stokes Worry It Would Be the Most Polluting Power Plant in the U.S.
items.summary: The tech giant is investing in the natural-gas-burning power plant as part of a huge data center in Texas, even as it pledges to honor climate commitments.

items.title: F.C.C. Removes Limit on Broadcast TV Ownership
items.summary: The move lifts a rule that said a single television-station owner could not reach more than 39 percent of U.S. households.

items.title: French Streamers Convicted in Case Related to Kick Livestream Death
items.summary: The two men, users of the platform Kick, received suspended sentences and fines.

items.title: Follow the Markets and Track Stocks With These Free Apps
items.summary: Google Finance and Apple’s Stocks app have added new features over the years to make them more useful for tracking the markets and your investments.

items.title: TikTok Lays Off 250 Employees in Office That Includes Content Moderation
items.summary: TikTok did not give a detailed reason for the layoffs, which will shutter its Nashville office.

items.summary: Jeff Dean, who for years was one of Google’s most important executives, is leading the new artificial intelligence company with the backing of Google.
